bibl.title: Representations of specific acoustic patterns in the auditory cortex and hippocampus
bibl.publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: where in the brain a freshly and implicitly learnt noise-like acoustic pattern is represented
span.quote: The objective of our study was to determine the neural substrate for the representation of freshly learnt acoustic patterns.

span.label: how the brain learns novel acoustic patterns, and whether a mechanism exists for storing acoustic patterns as such
span.quote: Although a number of brain imaging studies [ 1 – 4 ] have highlighted the brain system which represents the meaning of sounds, key questions remain as to how the brain learns novel acoustic patterns, and whether a specific mechanism exists for the storage of acoustic patterns per se .

span.label: shows that planum temporale and hippocampus, but not primary auditory cortex, carry activity patterns distinguishing three specific learnt noise exemplars
span.quote: We found that activity in planum temporale and the hippocampus reliably distinguished between the learnt acoustic patterns. Our results demonstrate that these structures are involved in the neural representation of specific acoustic patterns after they have been learnt.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Our results demonstrate that these structures are involved in the neural representation of specific acoustic patterns after they have been learnt.

span.label: implicit learning of random acoustic patterns
span.quote: Previous behavioural studies have shown that repeated presentation of a randomly chosen acoustic pattern leads to the unsupervised learning of some of its specific acoustic features.

span.label: fmri
span.quote: We used high-resolution functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and multi-voxel pattern analysis (MVPA).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A connected planum temporale-hippocampus system converts the dense HG activity pattern for a complex sound into a sparser representation that can be stored in long-term memory
span.quote: The purpose of such a system may be to transform the rich pattern of activity for complex sounds expressed in HG into sparser representations, more amenable to long-term memory storage.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Repeated exposure lays down a separate memory trace for each learnt exemplar in planum temporale and hippocampus, which is what the classifier reads out
span.quote: The most parsimonious explanation for our data is a unique memory trace in PT and HC that is formed for each of the three RefTCs, although more work will be needed to probe this point further.

span.label: the learning is made incidental by construction: one exemplar silently recurs across trials while every other stimulus is generated anew, so exposure is the only difference
span.quote: Without the subjects’ knowledge, however, one exemplar of a repeated tone cloud (reference tone cloud, RefTC) remained the same from trial to trial. That is, for the RefTC stimulus not only the same burst of tone cloud was repeated (three times) within a trial, but also the exact same exemplar reoccurred over several trials. The trials consisting of RefTC stimuli were presented randomly among trials of RTC and NTC. A RefTC stimulus was drawn from the same statistical process as any other RTC; the only difference was that the same exemplar of RefTC was presented across different trials.

span.label: the repeated and non-repeated stimuli are drawn from the same statistical process, so acoustic parameters cannot explain the difference
span.quote: Importantly, the repeatedly presented stimuli (RefTCs) and the non-repeated stimuli (RTC) were well balanced with respect to acoustic parameters. The key difference between the two conditions was in terms of exposure over the course of the experiment.

span.label: training is run inside the scanner while it is running, so the acoustic environment of learning matches that of testing
span.quote: All training occurred inside the MRI scanner while it was running in order to create the same conditions during learning as during subsequent testing.

span.label: the analysis was switched from univariate to multivariate after the first found nothing, and the switch is disclosed
span.quote: We initially used standard univariate analyses to interrogate the data, but did not find any significant difference in the mean activity evoked by the three RefTC stimuli in any part of the brain. We therefore focused on using MVPA which we believed would have increased sensitivity in our experimental context.

span.label: a boundary with no consensus in the literature is chosen explicitly rather than left implicit
span.quote: The markers for the posterior boundary of PT are not well established, because in most cases the posterior end of the sylvian fissure bifurcates into ascending and descending rami, the pattern of which varies across subjects [ 21 ]. There is no consensus on whether the posterior end of PT is limited to the posterior end of the horizontal portion of sylvian fissure [ 22 , 23 ] or extends all the way up to the end-point of the ascending ramus (which could cover a part of the parietal lobe [ 21 ]). In this study, we chose the latter option.

span.label: label shuffling is used to confirm the classifier is not exploiting some artefact of the design
span.quote: To ensure that the classifiers were unbiased and that classification was based on unique representations for each of the three RefTCs, we ran a control analysis in which we randomly shuffled (from trial to trial) the labels of the three RefTCs. The classifiers were trained and tested as above. As expected, the performance of the classifier dropped to chance level for all the brain regions

span.label: a second control classifies stimuli whose exemplar changes every trial, which should be undecodable if the effect really depends on repetition
span.quote: To further confirm that classification of RefTCs was based on stable representations (owing to the repeated presentation of the same exemplars), we ran a second control analysis. In this analysis, we divided the 60 RTC trials randomly into three classes and performed the same classification analysis. Since a different exemplar is presented in every trial of RTC, representation of RTC changes from trial to trial. It is therefore expected that the classifier should not be able to classify the RTC stimuli significantly better than chance.

span.label: regions of interest are hand-segmented per subject from that subject's own anatomy rather than warped to a template
span.quote: The markers for the posterior boundary of PT are not well established, because in most cases the posterior end of the sylvian fissure bifurcates into ascending and descending rami, the pattern of which varies across subjects [ 21 ]. There is no consensus on whether the posterior end of PT is limited to the posterior end of the horizontal portion of sylvian fissure [ 22 , 23 ] or extends all the way up to the end-point of the ascending ramus (which could cover a part of the parietal lobe [ 21 ]). In this study, we chose the latter option.

span.label: feature selection by searchlight is used to raise signal-to-noise before classification, fitted on the training split only
span.quote: The purpose of feature selection is to reduce the set of features (in this case, voxels) in a dataset to those most likely to carry relevant information. This is effectively the same as removing voxels most likely to carry noise and is a way of increasing the signal-to-noise ratio.

span.label: the sensory and timbre explanations are argued against by absence of precedent rather than by measurement, and the authors say so
span.quote: We considered whether our results might be explained by sensory or perceptual representations in PT and/or HC. The existence of sensory representations of fine spectro-temporal features that occurs in non-primary auditory cortex and HC but not in primary auditory cortex is unlikely. Mapping of the different perceptual timbre of different exemplars could occur in non-primary auditory cortex, but there is no precedent for any effect of manipulating spectro-temporal structure and timbre on hippocampal activity

span.label: the regions are predicted in advance with reasons, so the six-way comparison is hypothesis-driven rather than exploratory
span.quote: We also hypothesized that structures in the medial temporal lobes (MTLs) would be crucial. In addition to hippocampus (HC), which has been shown to have a role in long-term memory for sounds [ 15 , 16 ], we also speculated that entorhinal/perirhinal cortex (EPC) and parahippocampal cortex (PHC), both of which receive dense input from the non-primary auditory areas [ 17 ], may be involved.

span.label: The near-significant STS classification may reflect low statistical power, so an STS role cannot be excluded.
span.quote: This lack of significance may be owing to the low power of our study, so a role for STS in the learning of novel acoustic patterns cannot be ruled out.

span.label: The memory-trace interpretation of the PT and HC decoding is the most parsimonious account but is not established by these data alone.
span.quote: The most parsimonious explanation for our data is a unique memory trace in PT and HC that is formed for each of the three RefTCs, although more work will be needed to probe this point further.

span.label: The learning-phase fMRI data were not suitable for MVPA, so the time course of representation formation could not be examined.
span.quote: Our learning phase was optimized to facilitate acquisition of the three RefTCs; consequently, the fMRI data acquired during this phase were not intended (nor were they suitable) for analysis using MVPA, because our focus was solely on where the learnt RefTCs were represented.

span.label: awareness was probed with a single post-hoc question and two of seven listeners reported some, so the implicitness claim is hedged to some cases
span.quote: Subjective reports from the participants after the experiment showed that most were not aware of any stimulus re-occurring during the experiment, suggesting that in some cases the learning occurred implicitly.

span.label: the near-significant superior temporal sulcus result is attributed to low power, leaving a role there unexcluded
span.quote: This lack of significance may be owing to the low power of our study, so a role for STS in the learning of novel acoustic patterns cannot be ruled out.

span.label: the learning-phase scans were not suitable for the main analysis, so the time course of learning could not be examined
span.quote: Our learning phase was optimized to facilitate acquisition of the three RefTCs; consequently, the fMRI data acquired during this phase were not intended (nor were they suitable) for analysis using MVPA, because our focus was solely on where the learnt RefTCs were represented.

span.label: how many repetitions are needed to build a stable representation is unknown
span.quote: Further work is required to determine how many repetitions of each exemplar are required during the training phase before a stable representation is built in the PT and HC.

span.label: the direction of causal influence between the two regions is unresolved
span.quote: A further question concerns the direction of causal influences of the PT and HC on each other that occur during the construction of stable representations.

span.label: human auditory-to-medial-temporal connectivity is not fully known, so the anatomical argument rests on monkey work
span.quote: Structural connectivity between human auditory cortex and the MTLs is not completely understood.

span.label: the memory-trace interpretation is offered as the most parsimonious rather than as established
span.quote: The most parsimonious explanation for our data is a unique memory trace in PT and HC that is formed for each of the three RefTCs, although more work will be needed to probe this point further.

span.label: a linear support vector classifier with cross-validation and searchlight feature selection, used to ask whether a region distinguishes stimuli rather than whether it activates more
span.quote: The purpose of feature selection is to reduce the set of features (in this case, voxels) in a dataset to those most likely to carry relevant information. This is effectively the same as removing voxels most likely to carry noise and is a way of increasing the signal-to-noise ratio.

span.label: the repeated-noise paradigm, in which a silently recurring random exemplar reveals template learning through improved repetition detection
span.quote: However, without this being mentioned to subjects, there was in fact a third type of trials: one particular exemplar of repeated noise was presented over several trials, randomly interspersed throughout an experimental block. These trials (reference repeated noise, RefRN) were thus initially drawn from the same process as RN but, unlike RN, they were acoustically identical across several trials.

span.label: a control analysis with the class labels RANDOMLY SHUFFLED from trial to trial, run through the same classifier
span.quote: To ensure that the classifiers were unbiased and that classification was based on unique representations for each of the three RefTCs, we ran a control analysis in which we randomly shuffled

span.label: planum temporale - bounded at the horizontal sylvian fissure versus extending to the ascending ramus and into parietal lobe; no consensus exists and the choice is stipulated per study
span.quote: The markers for the posterior boundary of PT are not well established, because in most cases the posterior end of the sylvian fissure bifurcates into ascending and descending rami, the pattern of which varies across subjects [ 21 ]. There is no consensus on whether the posterior end of PT is limited to the posterior end of the horizontal portion of sylvian fissure [ 22 , 23 ] or extends all the way up to the end-point of the ascending ramus (which could cover a part of the parietal lobe [ 21 ]). In this study, we chose the latter option.

span.label: learning - explicit and reportable versus implicit; probed here with one debriefing question, and the conclusion hedged to some cases
span.quote: Subjective reports from the participants after the experiment showed that most were not aware of any stimulus re-occurring during the experiment, suggesting that in some cases the learning occurred implicitly.

span.label: the same acoustic structure - as a repeated stimulus within a trial versus as the same exemplar recurring across trials; the second is what produces learning and the first is the control
span.quote: Without the subjects’ knowledge, however, one exemplar of a repeated tone cloud (reference tone cloud, RefTC) remained the same from trial to trial. That is, for the RefTC stimulus not only the same burst of tone cloud was repeated (three times) within a trial, but also the exact same exemplar reoccurred over several trials. The trials consisting of RefTC stimuli were presented randomly among trials of RTC and NTC. A RefTC stimulus was drawn from the same statistical process as any other RTC; the only difference was that the same exemplar of RefTC was presented across different trials.

span.label: an analysis result - as absent under mean activation versus present under distributed pattern classification, on the same scans
span.quote: We initially used standard univariate analyses to interrogate the data, but did not find any significant difference in the mean activity evoked by the three RefTC stimuli in any part of the brain. We therefore focused on using MVPA which we believed would have increased sensitivity in our experimental context.

span.label: a representation of a sound - as a sensory or timbre code versus as a memory trace; the second is preferred on parsimony rather than measurement
span.quote: The most parsimonious explanation for our data is a unique memory trace in PT and HC that is formed for each of the three RefTCs, although more work will be needed to probe this point further.

span.label: replicates → Agus et al. [5]
span.quote: As in Agus et al. [ 5 ], the behavioural data in our study revealed better performance on repeated exemplars compared to performance on non-repeated exemplars confirming learning of acoustic patterns.

span.label: extends → the magnetoencephalography study [37] showing phase-pattern specificity for learnt noise exemplars
span.quote: However, compared to the results in [ 37 ], our results are more specific with respect to the areas of auditory cortex involved in storing pre-semantic-specific templates.

span.label: extends → visual-domain studies [39] showing hippocampal sensitivity to low-level perceptual features
span.quote: The results of our study further extend these results by showing that the HC is not only sensitive to low-level features of stimuli that are explicitly recalled, but also constructs representations that are specific to acoustic features which are learned implicitly.

span.label: extends → behavioural work showing that repeated presentation of a random noise exemplar produces unsupervised template learning
span.quote: The main result was that performance was considerably better for the RefRN stimuli than for the RN stimuli. Since the only difference between RefRN and RN was that RefRN was heard over several trials, the improved performance could be attributed to the learning of a template for RefRN.

span.label: extends → a magnetoencephalography study showing different phase patterns for different learnt noise exemplars, by localising the representation more specifically
span.quote: Although HC is known to be involved in processing of complex and meaningful sounds [ 15 , 38 ], to the best of our knowledge, our study is the first to demonstrate the encoding of noise-like acoustic patterns in the HC.

span.label: extends → visual work showing hippocampal sensitivity to low-level perceptual features, to implicitly learnt acoustic features
span.quote: The results of our study further extend these results by showing that the HC is not only sensitive to low-level features of stimuli that are explicitly recalled, but also constructs representations that are specific to acoustic features which are learned implicitly.

span.label: builds-on → the hypothesis that planum temporale generates acoustic templates at a stage before semantic processing
span.quote: Specifically, we predicted engagement of planum temporale (PT) which has been hypothesized to be involved in the generation of acoustic ‘templates’ at a stage before semantic processing [ 12 ] and superior temporal sulcus (STS), which has been shown to store long-term memories for sounds

span.label: builds-on → monkey tracing showing belt and parabelt, but not core, project directly to entorhinal cortex
span.quote: However, the connectivity pattern between auditory cortex and the MTL of monkeys [ 47 ] (for review, see [ 17 ]) shows that belt and parabelt, but not the core, of the auditory cortex have direct projections to the entorhinal cortex.

span.label: supports → evidence that primary auditory cortex stores long-term representations of specific auditory experiences
span.quote: Given evidence for the involvement of primary auditory cortex in storing long-term representations of specific auditory experiences [ 9 – 11 ], we hypothesized that Heschl's gyrus (HG), which contains primary auditory cortex, would be involved.

span.label: reference tone cloud —contrasted-with→ repeated tone cloud
span.quote: Without the subjects’ knowledge, however, one exemplar of a repeated tone cloud (reference tone cloud, RefTC) remained the same from trial to trial. That is, for the RefTC stimulus not only the same burst of tone cloud was repeated (three times) within a trial, but also the exact same exemplar reoccurred over several trials. The trials consisting of RefTC stimuli were presented randomly among trials of RTC and NTC. A RefTC stimulus was drawn from the same statistical process as any other RTC; the only difference was that the same exemplar of RefTC was presented across different trials.

span.label: planum temporale —is-a→ computational hub
span.quote: The availability of pattern specific information in the PT is consistent with a role as a computational hub [ 12 ], where spectro-temporal patterns are matched with learned patterns that are stored beyond the auditory cortex.

span.label: planum temporale —contrasted-with→ Heschl's gyrus
span.quote: We found that patterns of activity across voxels in PT, but not in HG, could distinguish between the three learned acoustic patterns. We speculate that this might reflect a type of representation within PT that is not a simple representation of acoustic pattern but a more refined representation that requires interaction with HC (see below).

span.label: multi-voxel pattern analysis —operationalised-as→ support vector machine
span.quote: Multi-voxel pattern analysis was used to test if the learnt acoustic patterns could be ‘decoded’ from the patterns of activity in the auditory cortex and medial temporal lobe.

span.label: superior temporal sulcus —causes→ categorical perception
span.quote: From the auditory perception point of view, converging evidence from neuroimaging studies show that STS is involved in categorical perception of speech [ 13 ] and non-speech [ 14 , 41 ] auditory stimuli.

span.label: hippocampus —causes→ memory trace
span.quote: The most parsimonious explanation for our data is a unique memory trace in PT and HC that is formed for each of the three RefTCs, although more work will be needed to probe this point further.

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Given that we were interested in whether results were significantly above chance, one tailed t -tests were used.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Repeated measures ANOVAs were used to compare accuracy values between regions, and subsequently interrogated using two-tailed paired t -tests.

span.label: cross-validation
span.quote: The overall classification procedure involved splitting the fMRI data into two segments: a ‘training’ set used to train a classifier with fixed regularization hyperparameter C = 1, and a ‘test’ set used to independently test the classification performance using a standard 10-fold cross-validation testing procedure.

span.label: p-value
span.quote: A threshold of p < 0.05 was employed throughout.

span.label: support vector machine classification
span.quote: A linear support vector machine (SVM) classifier was created for each ROI.

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: Mean volumes (in cubic millimetre, summed across both hemispheres) and standard deviations (SD) for the region of interests (ROIs) were as follows: HC 4188.8 (472.97), EPC 5026.04 (488.71), PHC 1799.29 (256.69), HG 2317.93 (521.93), PT 3967.07 (719.66) and STS 14396.07 (2476.29).

span.label: d-prime (signal detection sensitivity)
span.quote: Post hoc analysis showed that dprimes for the three RefTC were greater than RTC (RefTC-1 > RTC: t 6 = 2.93, p = 0.02; RefTC-2 > RTC: t 6 = 5.12, p = 0.002; RefTC-3 > RTC: t 6 = 2.97, p = 0.02).

span.label: multi-voxel pattern analysis
span.quote: Multi-voxel pattern analysis was used to test if the learnt acoustic patterns could be ‘decoded’ from the patterns of activity in the auditory cortex and medial temporal lobe.

span.label: linear support vector machine
span.quote: The purpose of feature selection is to reduce the set of features (in this case, voxels) in a dataset to those most likely to carry relevant information. This is effectively the same as removing voxels most likely to carry noise and is a way of increasing the signal-to-noise ratio.

span.label: one tailed t -tests
span.quote: The classifier accuracy values for each brain region were compared to chance, which in this case was 33% as we were classifying between three exemplars. Given that we were interested in whether results were significantly above chance, one tailed t -tests were used.

span.label: Repeated measures ANOVAs
span.quote: The classifier accuracy values for each brain region were compared to chance, which in this case was 33% as we were classifying between three exemplars. Given that we were interested in whether results were significantly above chance, one tailed t -tests were used.

span.label: dprimes
span.quote: Analysis of behavioural performance during testing showed a significant effect of stimulus on dprimes ( F 3,18 = 8.98, p = 0.001).

span.label: Of six regions of interest, only the hippocampus and planum temporale allowed a classifier to tell apart which of the three learnt tone-cloud exemplars was being heard; HG, entorhinal/perirhinal cortex and parahippocampal cortex did not.
span.quote: Only two regions, HC and PT, showed performance above chance: (HC: t 6 = 2.711, p = 0.018; EPC: t 6 = 0.188, p = 0.43; PHC: t 6 = 0.117, p = 0.46; HG: t 6 = 0.620, p = 0.28; PT: t 6 = 5.106, p = 0.001; STS: t 6 = 1.715, p = 0.07).

span.label: Subjects detected repetition better for all three repeatedly presented reference tone clouds than for freshly generated repeated tone clouds, showing that the specific patterns had been learnt.
span.quote: Post hoc comparison revealed better performance on all the RefTC stimuli compared to RTC (RefTC-1 > RTC, t 6 = 3.96, p = 0.007; RefTC-2 > RTC, t 6 = 4.30, p = 0.005; RefTC-3 > RTC, t 6 = 5.43, p = 0.001).

span.label: Standard univariate analysis found no difference in mean activity between the three learnt patterns anywhere in the brain, so the effect existed only in the multi-voxel activity pattern.
span.quote: We initially used standard univariate analyses to interrogate the data, but did not find any significant difference in the mean activity evoked by the three RefTC stimuli in any part of the brain.

span.label: When the 60 trial-unique repeated tone clouds were split into three arbitrary classes, classification fell to chance in every region, confirming that decoding depended on stable repeated exemplars rather than on stimulus class labels.
span.quote: As predicted, the classifier performance was at chance for all ROIs, (HC: t 6 = −0.058, p = 0.955; EPC: t 6 = −0.421, p = 0.689; PHG: t 6 = 0.953, p = 0.377; HG: t 6 = 1.365, p = 0.221; PT: t 6 = −0.174, p = 0.868; STS: t 6 = −0.316, p = 0.763).

span.label: Most participants did not notice that any sound had recurred across trials, indicating the learning was implicit.
span.quote: Subjective reports from the participants after the experiment showed that most were not aware of any stimulus re-occurring during the experiment, suggesting that in some cases the learning occurred implicitly.

span.label: The authors claim this is the first demonstration that the hippocampus encodes noise-like acoustic patterns that carry no semantic content.
span.quote: Although HC is known to be involved in processing of complex and meaningful sounds [ 15 , 38 ], to the best of our knowledge, our study is the first to demonstrate the encoding of noise-like acoustic patterns in the HC.

span.label: only hippocampus and planum temporale classified the three learnt exemplars above chance
span.quote: Only two regions, HC and PT, showed performance above chance: (HC: t 6 = 2.711, p = 0.018; EPC: t 6 = 0.188, p = 0.43; PHC: t 6 = 0.117, p = 0.46; HG: t 6 = 0.620, p = 0.28; PT: t 6 = 5.106, p = 0.001; STS: t 6 = 1.715, p = 0.07).

span.label: planum temporale carried more information than HG, entorhinal/perirhinal and parahippocampal cortex, and hippocampus more than HG
span.quote: A repeated measures ANOVA showed a significant effect for region ( F 5,30 = 3.271, p = 0.018), which was driven by more information being present in the HC when compared with HG (HC > HG: t 6 = 2.765, p = 0.033) as well as more information present in PT when compared with HG, EPC and PHC (PT > HG: t 6 = 4.182, p = 0.006; PT > EPC: t 6 = 3.059, p = 0.022; PT > PHC: t 6 = 3.291, p = 0.017).

span.label: primary auditory cortex did not distinguish the learnt patterns
span.quote: We found that patterns of activity across voxels in PT, but not in HG, could distinguish between the three learned acoustic patterns. We speculate that this might reflect a type of representation within PT that is not a simple representation of acoustic pattern but a more refined representation that requires interaction with HC (see below).

span.label: superior temporal sulcus fell just short of significance at p = 0.07
span.quote: Only two regions, HC and PT, showed performance above chance: (HC: t 6 = 2.711, p = 0.018; EPC: t 6 = 0.188, p = 0.43; PHC: t 6 = 0.117, p = 0.46; HG: t 6 = 0.620, p = 0.28; PT: t 6 = 5.106, p = 0.001; STS: t 6 = 1.715, p = 0.07).

span.label: detection was better for the silently repeated exemplars than for matched non-repeated ones, confirming learning
span.quote: Analysis of behavioural performance during testing showed a significant effect of stimulus on dprimes ( F 3,18 = 8.98, p = 0.001).

span.label: shuffling the exemplar labels dropped classification to chance in every region
span.quote: To ensure that the classifiers were unbiased and that classification was based on unique representations for each of the three RefTCs, we ran a control analysis in which we randomly shuffled (from trial to trial) the labels of the three RefTCs. The classifiers were trained and tested as above. As expected, the performance of the classifier dropped to chance level for all the brain regions

span.label: classifying non-repeated stimuli, whose exemplar changes each trial, was also at chance everywhere
span.quote: To further confirm that classification of RefTCs was based on stable representations (owing to the repeated presentation of the same exemplars), we ran a second control analysis. In this analysis, we divided the 60 RTC trials randomly into three classes and performed the same classification analysis. Since a different exemplar is presented in every trial of RTC, representation of RTC changes from trial to trial. It is therefore expected that the classifier should not be able to classify the RTC stimuli significantly better than chance.

span.label: five of seven listeners reported no awareness that any sound recurred; one said yes and one said some
span.quote: After the MRI scanning, listeners were debriefed by means of a questionnaire. In particular, a question was asked as to whether they thought that any of the sounds recurred during the experiment. One listener said yes, one said some and the remaining five said no.

span.label: univariate analysis found no difference in mean activity anywhere in the brain
span.quote: We initially used standard univariate analyses to interrogate the data, but did not find any significant difference in the mean activity evoked by the three RefTC stimuli in any part of the brain. We therefore focused on using MVPA which we believed would have increased sensitivity in our experimental context.

span.label: no hemispheric difference in classification accuracy in any region, so data were collapsed across hemispheres
span.quote: Only two regions, HC and PT, showed performance above chance: (HC: t 6 = 2.711, p = 0.018; EPC: t 6 = 0.188, p = 0.43; PHC: t 6 = 0.117, p = 0.46; HG: t 6 = 0.620, p = 0.28; PT: t 6 = 5.106, p = 0.001; STS: t 6 = 1.715, p = 0.07).

span.label: this is reported as the first demonstration of noise-like acoustic patterns encoded in the hippocampus
span.quote: Although HC is known to be involved in processing of complex and meaningful sounds [ 15 , 38 ], to the best of our knowledge, our study is the first to demonstrate the encoding of noise-like acoustic patterns in the HC.

span.label: reference tone cloud (RefTC)
span.quote: Without the subjects’ knowledge, however, one exemplar of a repeated tone cloud (reference tone cloud, RefTC) remained the same from trial to trial.

span.label: tone clouds
span.quote: These are noise-like stimuli with a coarser spectro-temporal structure than white noise that allows them to be perceived easily under scanning conditions [ 18 ].

span.label: feature selection
span.quote: The purpose of feature selection is to reduce the set of features (in this case, voxels) in a dataset to those most likely to carry relevant information.

span.label: categorical perception
span.quote: Categorical perception involves mapping a continuum of variation for low-level acoustic features of the stimuli into a discrete number of abstract categories.

span.label: tone clouds
span.quote: The stimuli were ‘tone clouds’. These are noise-like stimuli with a coarser spectro-temporal structure than white noise that allows them to be perceived easily under scanning conditions

span.label: reference tone cloud
span.quote: Without the subjects’ knowledge, however, one exemplar of a repeated tone cloud (reference tone cloud, RefTC) remained the same from trial to trial. That is, for the RefTC stimulus not only the same burst of tone cloud was repeated (three times) within a trial, but also the exact same exemplar reoccurred over several trials. The trials consisting of RefTC stimuli were presented randomly among trials of RTC and NTC. A RefTC stimulus was drawn from the same statistical process as any other RTC; the only difference was that the same exemplar of RefTC was presented across different trials.

span.label: feature selection
span.quote: The purpose of feature selection is to reduce the set of features (in this case, voxels) in a dataset to those most likely to carry relevant information. This is effectively the same as removing voxels most likely to carry noise and is a way of increasing the signal-to-noise ratio.

span.label: Categorical perception
span.quote: Categorical perception involves mapping a continuum of variation for low-level acoustic features of the stimuli into a discrete number of abstract categories.

span.label: template
span.quote: However, before a label is assigned, the auditory system must first learn a ‘template’ corresponding to the specific acoustic structure.

span.label: repetition of the same tone-cloud exemplar across trials (RefTC versus RTC)
span.term: repetition of the same tone-cloud exemplar across trials (RefTC versus RTC)
span.quote: A RefTC stimulus was drawn from the same statistical process as any other RTC; the only difference was that the same exemplar of RefTC was presented across different trials.

span.label: MVPA classification accuracy across voxels in each region of interest
span.term: MVPA classification accuracy across voxels in each region of interest
span.quote: This therefore generated 10 sets of SVM training and test sets that produced overall classification accuracy from the proportion of correct classification ‘guesses’ across all 10-folds of the cross-validation.

span.label: behavioural repetition-detection sensitivity (dprime)
span.quote: Analysis of behavioural performance during testing showed a significant effect of stimulus on dprimes ( F 3,18 = 8.98, p = 0.001).

span.label: acoustic parameters of the stimuli
span.quote: Importantly, the repeatedly presented stimuli (RefTCs) and the non-repeated stimuli (RTC) were well balanced with respect to acoustic parameters.
